points.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO.
points.body: Huang stepped down after reports of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, with Colette Kress named CEO and Congress opening a second investigation into Nvidia's China sales. Founders and VCs expect smaller checks for AI startups without his backing, and some ask whether Nvidia's open-source push will last.

points.headline: China's top AI models were trained on export-banned Nvidia chips.
points.body: A forensic report by an ex-OpenAI engineer finds Blackwell fingerprints in models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group. Nvidia had privately told a US lawmaker that tracking chips to stop smuggling is technically possible, while its industry group called it infeasible.

points.headline: ChatGPT Wallet lets agents buy things for you.
points.body: OpenAI's new Wallet lets agents in ChatGPT, Codex and Dots complete purchases with the user's approval, starting with US Pro subscribers and major US cards. Agentic commerce is becoming a stack of its own, and Amazon is building a graph of the world's product data for AI search.

points.headline: Google ships Gemini 4 Hydrogen and puts it in Search.
points.body: Gemini 4 Hydrogen replaces 3.8 Flash in a fast, broad rollout, unlike the slower releases of Carbon and Argon. In Search, AI Mode now handles complex questions better, with more relevant links and richer visual answers.

points.headline: World-action models arrive for robots.
points.body: Nvidia's GR00T 2 predicts future video and robot actions together so skills can move between machines, and Runway's Praxis-1 is now available with open weights. Rhoda AI takes the same route, training general robot models on video data.

points.headline: Local AI hits 1.0: llama.cpp and ggml.
points.body: llama.cpp and its ggml library reached version 1.0, a stable base for running models on your own hardware. Open-weight models keep pace: Unsloth published new Qwen3.8-27B quantizations, and a retrained Qwen3.8 can now say things Chinese authorities don't like.
